title: Scientific method
content: Science develops and tests explanations using observations, hypotheses, methods, evidence, analysis, and replication. A hypothesis should be testable and expose what evidence could support or challenge it. Conclusions should match the limits of the data.

title: Chemistry: atoms and bonds
content: Atoms contain protons, neutrons, and electrons. Elements are defined by proton number. Chemical bonds and interactions involve electron arrangements; ionic bonding involves attraction between charged ions, while covalent bonding involves shared electron pairs.

title: Chemical reactions and conservation
content: Chemical reactions rearrange atoms into new substances. Balanced equations conserve atoms of each element and reflect mass conservation in ordinary chemical reactions. Reaction classes include synthesis, decomposition, single displacement, double displacement, and combustion; classification depends on reactants and products.

title: Physics: energy
content: Energy is a conserved quantity in an isolated system. Kinetic energy for nonrelativistic motion is K=mv²/2; gravitational potential near Earth's surface is U=mgh relative to a chosen level. Work is energy transferred by force acting through displacement; power is energy transfer per time.

title: Biology: cells
content: Cells are basic units of life. The membrane regulates exchange; DNA stores hereditary information; ribosomes synthesize proteins. In eukaryotes, mitochondria participate in cellular respiration and ATP production, while chloroplasts in plants and algae perform photosynthesis.

title: Photosynthesis and respiration
content: Photosynthesis uses light energy to build energy-rich organic molecules from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen in oxygenic photosynthesis. Cellular respiration extracts chemical energy from molecules such as glucose and transfers it to ATP; pathways and oxygen requirements vary by organism and process.

title: Measurement and experimental controls
content: Accuracy is closeness to a reference; precision is repeatability or consistency. Independent variables are manipulated, dependent variables measured, and controls help isolate effects. Replicates, calibrated instruments, and documented methods improve reliability.

title: Correlation and causation
content: Correlation indicates that variables co-vary; it does not alone show one causes the other. Confounders, reverse causation, selection effects, or coincidence can explain an association. Causal claims require design and evidence suited to the question.
